blacklistabilityReview.evidence: USDD's canonical Tron, Ethereum, and BSC direct implementations expose wards for mint, rely, and deny, but transfer and burn require holder authority or allowance and contain no blacklist, holder freeze, seizure, or pause mechanism; the Ethereum and BSC deployments are non-proxy. The upstream result instead comes from the debt-weighted all-chain reserve review captured 2026-08-10: 62.2% of minted USDD debt is backed through Smart Allocator positions itemized as USDS, USDT, USDT0, and USDC, and another 8.3% uses direct USDT PSM/vault issuance rails. That 70.5% freeze-exposed majority exceeds the v3.9973 threshold and resolves USDD as Upstream rather than direct Yes.

oracleRisk.summary: USDD CDP collateral prices pass through per-collateral Median, OSM, and Spot modules before reaching Vat, with Chainlink and WinkLink documented as the primary feed sources.

branchApplicability.rationale: USDD supports governed CDP collateral types with per-ilk oracle modules, collateral ratios, liquidation parameters, and auction contracts. The documented collateral types share one Median-to-OSM-to-Spot and Dog-to-Clipper mechanism family; PSM stablecoin conversion is a fixed-price issuance rail rather than a collateral-liquidation branch.

branches.label: USDD governed CDP collateral types
branches.summary: Governed USDD collateral types share per-ilk Median, OSM, and Spot pricing followed by Dog and collateral-specific Clipper liquidation auctions.

feeds.path: Supported feeds -> per-collateral Median -> OSM current/next price -> Spot -> Vat

branches.fallbackBehavior: The OSM retains a current value and separately stages the next Median value; if updates stop, Vat continues using the last Spot value and the collateral price can become stale.

collateralParameters.note: Each collateral type has a governed Spot liquidation ratio and Dog liquidation capacity; USDD documentation states the minimum ratio varies by asset and illustrates a 130% liquidation threshold.

branches.liquidationMechanism: When a Vault falls below its collateral-specific minimum ratio, Dog initiates liquidation and the corresponding Clipper sells collateral through a descending-price Dutch auction; proceeds repay USDD debt and penalties and surplus collateral returns to the user.
branches.backstop: Collateral-auction proceeds cover Vault debt; the documented system architecture provides Vow accounting and a Flop debt-auction path that sells governance tokens to recapitalize a protocol deficit.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: Uncovered system deficits can proceed to the documented debt-auction path. Deployment records also identify End and ESM contracts on supported CDP chains for emergency shutdown and settlement.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Material USDD supply on Tron, Ethereum, and BSC uses chain-local native token and Join rails. Legacy BTTC predicate representations remain peripheral bridge risk and are not treated as canonical issuance.
